subject: [AMBER] Insights for understanding the flags in input files

messages.author: Priyasha Majee
messages.body:
Dear Sir/madam
I am a beginner in MD. when i am reading the input scripts, i am unable
to understand the significance of flags used and their values.
Heating Equilibration - constant volume
&cntrl
imin   = 0,
irest  = 0,
ntx    = 1,
ntb    = 1,
cut    = 10.0,
ntr    = 0,
ntc    = 2,
ntf    = 2,
tempi  = 0.0,
temp0  = 300.0,
ntt    = 3,
ig     = -1,
ioutfm = 1,
iwrap  = 1,
gamma_ln = 1.0,
nstlim = 1000000, dt = 0.002
ntpr = 1000, ntwx = 1000, ntwr = 1000
/
what does ntt , ig, ioutfm, ntx ,ntb, ntc,ntf mean?
i have read the manual several times. but cant grasp the idea for their
usage.
simple explanation for WHY and WHEN these flags are used is appreciated.
thanks in advance.

messages.author: Domenico Marson
messages.body:
Dear Priyasha,
I don’t want to seem rude, but a simple search of the manual for the term
“ioutfm” will lead you to the section in which all this flags are explained.
The question is too broad to be answered in a mailing list like that, and
can be answered with a proper look at the manual (and a search in this
mailing list for example for the explanation on why it is usually a good
idea to set ig to -1, if you don’t need an exact replicate of a simulation).
You should came back with a more defined question if you will still have
any more specific doubt about the proper value for some of these flags.
Just my 2 cents, I don’t want to seem rude, but just help you help yourself
to grow in this fascinating field :-)
